transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brought you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Well, my family brought me in. They say I’m here because I... I used up our savings. I bought a lot of wood, lights, and display stuff for the yard. 

I just kept pushing the work, you know, staying out there way after dark building it all. They're upset about the money, but... I just felt like if I stopped, the whole house and the whole block would lose its chance. I had to keep going.
Have you been using any alcohol, drugs, or other substances more than usual recently?
No, I haven't. I don't really drink, and I definitely don't mess with any drugs or anything like that. It was just me out there working, plain and simple. I haven't taken anything.
During this time, have you experienced anything unusual like hearing voices others don't hear, or having beliefs—like feeling you have special powers or a special mission—that others say aren't true?

Well, I don't hear any voices. But about the special mission... I know my family thinks I’m just mixed up right now. But I'm absolutely sure this neighborhood was picked for my last big civic art piece. That's why I was building all of it. 

And it's not just me making it up. I see the proof around me. Just little things, like... like the trucks slowing down when they pass by the house, or the neighbors looking over the fence at me. It proves they know it, too. They know something big is happening.
Have you ever had a period in the past—lasting at least a couple of weeks—where you felt unusually depressed, low on energy, or lost interest in things, separate from how you're feeling now?

No, I can't say that I have. I mean, everybody gets a little down now and then, but... no, not for weeks at a time like you're saying. I've never really been the type to just sit around with no energy or lose interest in what I'm doing. I usually just keep myself pretty busy and get on with things.

Aside from what's happening now, have you ever had another period in the past—lasting several days or more—where you felt unusually elevated, extremely energetic, or irritable, and needed much less sleep than usual?

No, I can't recall anything like that. I mean, I've always been a pretty steady guy. I worked hard all my life and got my rest when I needed it. I've never had a time before this where I was just running on no sleep or feeling all wound up for days on end. This whole thing right now... it's really a first for me.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a first-episode manic syndrome characterized by excessive goal-directed activity (extensive building/decorating), reckless spending depleting savings, decreased need for sleep (working late into the night), and grandiosity. Psychotic features are present, including a grandiose delusion (belief that his neighborhood was specially chosen for his 'civic art piece') and delusional misinterpretation of neutral environmental cues (trucks slowing, neighbors looking) as confirmatory evidence—consistent with ideas of reference/persecutory-grandiose delusions congruent with mood. No hallucinations were reported. Substance use was denied, ruling out substance-induced mood disorder. No prior depressive episodes were identified, arguing against Bipolar I Disorder (current episode) diagnosis of recurrent type, and no prior manic episodes were reported, confirming this is a single manic episode with psychotic features, coded as F30.2 rather than F31.2 (which requires a history of previous mood episodes). Schizophrenia (F20.0) is less likely given the mood-congruent nature of the delusions, the clear temporal association with elevated mood/energy, and absence of first-rank psychotic symptoms or chronic prodrome.
